column2: Smear-positive pulmonary TB: rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for 2 months, then RI for 4 months, with pyridoxine.
Unresectable stage III NSCLC: radical (chemo)radiotherapy followed by immunotherapy; radiotherapy also palliates haemoptysis.
Confirmed PE: immediate anticoagulation; LMWH here (DOAC preferred by NICE where suitable). Warfarin alone is too slow.
Tension pneumothorax: immediate needle decompression in the 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line (or 4th/5th anterior axillary), then drain.
Unresectable small cell lung cancer: platinum–etoposide chemotherapy (± immunotherapy), the tumour being highly chemosensitive.
Atopic child with 6 months of night cough and wheeze: paediatric low-dose ICS plus as-needed SABA.
Leaf-shaped calcified plaques crossing lobar boundaries in a well man are benign pleural plaques: no management required.
Snoring with GCS 6 and no gag reflex: insert an oropharyngeal (Guedel) airway; intubate if consciousness does not improve.
Semi-conscious with clenched jaw and intact gag: a nasopharyngeal airway is tolerated; an oral airway would provoke gagging.
Out-of-hospital collapse without equipment: open the airway with head tilt and chin lift, then check breathing and start CPR.
Failed intubation and bag-mask ventilation from laryngeal oedema ('can't intubate, can't oxygenate'): cricothyroidotomy.
During arrest, non-intubators use a supraglottic airway (laryngeal mask/i-gel) with minimal interruption to compressions.
Fever, pleuritic pain and rusty sputum with lobar consolidation in a young adult is pneumococcal pneumonia.
Cavitating pneumonia with abscesses after influenza is characteristic of S. aureus.
Dry cough with exertional desaturation and perihilar shadowing in HIV is Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
Pneumonia after travel with myalgia, dry cough and hyponatraemia causing a seizure suggests Legionella; urinary antigen.
Atypical pneumonia with hepatosplenomegaly in a parrot owner is psittacosis (C. psittaci); doxycycline.
Atopic child with nocturnal cough and wheeze: start paediatric low-dose ICS plus as-needed SABA.
Uncontrolled on high-dose ICS + LABA (after checking adherence and technique): add montelukast; refer if still poor.
Uncontrolled on high-dose ICS, LABA and montelukast: lowest-dose oral steroid under specialist care; consider biologics.
Too breathless to talk, HR 115, RR 36 is acute severe asthma: oxygen to 94–98%, nebulised salbutamol (+ ipratropium) and steroids.
Silent chest with PEF 30% despite initial treatment is life-threatening: IV magnesium 1.2–2 g and early ICU referral.
Paroxysmal coughing with cyanosis and post-tussive vomiting for months in an unimmunised child is pertussis; macrolide and notify.
Sudden cough in a well afebrile toddler with unilateral reduced breath sounds is an inhaled foreign body; rigid bronchoscopy.
Barking cough and stridor with mild fever in a toddler is croup (parainfluenza); oral dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg.
Rapid high fever, drooling, upright posture and soft stridor in an unimmunised child is epiglottitis (Hib): secure the airway, don't examine the throat.
Coryza progressing to cough, wheeze and widespread crackles in an infant is bronchiolitis (RSV); supportive care.
Under 65, alert, urea ≤ 7, RR < 30 and normal BP: CURB-65 = 0, home treatment with amoxicillin.
Confusion, urea > 7, RR ≥ 30, SBP < 90 and age ≥ 65: CURB-65 = 5, high severity.
Pneumonia needs new radiological shadowing; with a clear CXR this is a lower respiratory tract infection, not pneumonia.
Urea > 7, RR ≥ 30 and age ≥ 65 score (BP and AMTS 9 do not): CURB-65 = 3, high severity.
Only urea > 7 scores: CURB-65 = 1, low severity, usually home treatment.
Adults with CF are chronically colonised by Pseudomonas aeruginosa; exacerbations need two IV antipseudomonal agents.
Haemophilus influenzae, a Gram-negative coccobacillus, is the commonest bacterium in COPD exacerbations.
Drug injectors with fever and breathlessness have S. aureus (tricuspid IE, septic emboli); blood cultures and echo.
Dry cough, fever and diarrhoea after a hotel stay is Legionella; check sodium, LFTs and urinary antigen.
Rifampicin is a potent hepatic enzyme inducer (reduces warfarin, pill, steroids) and turns secretions orange.
Ethambutol causes optic neuritis with red–green colour blindness; check vision before and during treatment.
MSSA pneumonia in a drug injector: high-dose IV flucloxacillin (vancomycin if MRSA).
Metronidazole adds anaerobic cover to amoxicillin in aspiration pneumonia with foul sputum.
Painful swollen wrists and ankles in lung cancer is hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy (periostitis, usually with clubbing).
Shoulder pain down the inner arm with haemoptysis is a Pancoast tumour invading the brachial plexus (C8–T1).
Sudden flexural velvety pigmentation in an older adult is acanthosis nigricans, a paraneoplastic marker.
Ptosis, miosis and apparent enophthalmos is Horner syndrome from an apical tumour.
Proximal weakness with reflexes returning after contraction in small cell cancer is Lambert–Eaton syndrome (anti-VGCC).
Permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchioles with wall destruction defines emphysema.
Abrupt winter fever, myalgia and dry cough is influenza; oseltamivir for at-risk patients within 48 h.
Hoarseness, barking cough and stridor is laryngotracheobronchitis (croup); oral dexamethasone.
Chronic purulent sputum in cystic fibrosis reflects bronchiectasis; physiotherapy and culture-guided antibiotics.
Self-limiting productive cough with transient wheeze after a cold and a normal CXR is acute bronchitis; no antibiotics.
Basal subpleural reticulation with honeycombing is a UIP pattern, diagnostic of IPF in the right setting.
Cough and breathlessness with fluffy nodular shadowing in a farmer is extrinsic allergic alveolitis (farmer's lung).
FEV1/FVC 62% with only 60 mL (4%) reversibility in a smoker indicates COPD.
Cavitating nodules with haemoptysis and PR3-ANCA are granulomatosis with polyangiitis; steroids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide.
Hyper-resonance and reduced breath sounds after blunt trauma with a central trachea and stable BP is a simple pneumothorax; chest drain.
Stony dullness with absent breath sounds in a smoker with weight loss is a (likely malignant) pleural effusion; aspirate for cytology.
A recurrent episode with unilateral reduced breath sounds and an asymmetric CXR is recurrent primary pneumothorax; refer for surgery.
Clubbing, basal crackles and pleural disease after asbestos textile work is asbestosis; the bulky hilum needs CT for cancer.
Exertional dyspnoea, angina and syncope with a slow-rising pulse is severe aortic stenosis; normal PEF and D-dimer argue against asthma and PE.
Loss of the right heart border with neutrophilia is right middle lobe pneumonia; a normal D-dimer makes PE unlikely.
Stony dullness with a meniscus obscuring the hemidiaphragm is a pleural effusion; tap for cytology (cancer or mesothelioma).
Late ventilator-associated pneumonia (> 5 days) is commonly Pseudomonas; antipseudomonal therapy per local policy.
Pneumonia with multiple small abscesses in a fit young man is S. aureus (possibly PVL); antistaphylococcal plus anti-toxin agents.
A cluster of severe pneumonia among workers at one site suggests Legionella from contaminated water; notify.
A lactose-fermenting Gram-negative bacillus in blood and urine after bowel surgery is E. coli.
Fever, pleuritic pain, rusty sputum and segmental consolidation in a healthy adult is pneumococcal pneumonia.
